# Review — kebra-nagast-ch21-22

## Pass 1

Reviewer pass 1. Read: conventions.md, runbook.md, packet.md, units.json, known-forms.json, kebra-nagast-ch1.json, kebra-nagast-ch17-20.json (plus a grep of the other published parts for "Sheba"). No modern translation opened or recalled. Dillmann is unavailable: every word below marked unresolved stays unresolved for that reason. Units are numbered from 1 in file order (22 units); the "unit 10, ~62 words" of the brief is unit 11 here (index 10).

Checks that came out clean
- `t` joined equals the packet Geʿez exactly (1858 characters, whitespace aside); `t` and `p` flags untouched by the script (verified against a copy made before editing). Schema, keys, titleEn and part unchanged; only `l`, `i`, `n` and `about` were edited, by a script, never retyping Geʿez in `t`.
- Original to `l`, word by word, for all 22 units: no word dropped or added (differences only in suffix transparency, listed below).
- Numerals: ፳፩ 21, ፳፪ 22, ፩ 1, ፭፻ ወ፳ 520, ፸ወ፫ 73 all correct.
- Names: Solomon, Jerusalem, Tamrin (heading ታምሪን and body ተምሪን both noted), Aswan, Arabia, Ethiopia consistent with published parts and conventions.
- Unit 11 (the ~62-word unit): confirmed 62 words with exactly one terminal mark (the final ። after a stray ፡); there is no ፤ or ፨ inside, so there is no legitimate cut point under the "units end at ። ፤ ፨" rule. It stays whole. (Units 13 and 21, 41 words each, are within the ~45 limit.)
- Scriptural claims: Matthew 12:42 and Luke 11:31 (queen of the south rises in the judgment with this generation; came from the uttermost parts of the earth to hear Solomon's wisdom), 1 Kings 10:27 and 2 Chronicles 1:15 (silver as stones, cedar as sycamores), 1 Kings 10:23 and 3:12, Psalm 78:2 (77:2 LXX, "open my mouth in a parable", quoted of Christ in Matthew 13:35), Psalm 19:10, Deuteronomy 1:17, Proverbs 24:23, Proverbs 1:7, Acts 8:27 are accurate and, with the changes below, hedged as echoes or compare-notes rather than quotations. 1 Kings 5–6 / 2 Chronicles 2 for the Temple building is accurate.

### Changes (unit · field · severity · what was wrong · what was done)

Moderate (12)
1. U1 · n · moderate · Said the "Queen of Sheba of the book's earlier chapters" and that the Sheba identification "is the author's own". No earlier published part mentions Sheba (grep of ch1, 2–8, 9–12, 13–16, 17–20), and the identification of the Gospels' queen with the queen of Sheba is traditional, not the author's. Also asserted that አዜብ is "the Geʿez word" of the Gospels without a check. · Reworded: no earlier part names her; the traditional identification (1 Kings 10) is not made in these chapters; Gospel spelling "not checked".
2. U2 · n · moderate · Asserted ውእቱ "repeats the subject" and is the Ethiopian king, as the only reading. ውእቱ may equally be a resumptive "that" taking the whole clause as the object of ረከብኩ. · Gave both readings; referent kept as uncertain. `l`/`i` unchanged (both readings fit).
3. U9 · l, i, n · moderate · ህንደኬ rendered flatly "India", but the published ch17–20 spells India ህንድ (glossed "India"), so ህንደኬ is a different spelling (and the same as the Candace of Acts 8:27). · `l` and `i` now "India(?)"; note says it is not the ህንድ of ch. 20 and that the Acts 8:27 spelling is from memory, unchecked.
4. U13 · l, i, n · moderate · ሣ is the ሠ-series (ś), but the unknown word was transliterated "[ṣāʾṣāʾa]" (ṣ). · Changed to "[śāʾśāʾa]" in all three fields; note now says Dillmann is unavailable.
5. U14 · n · moderate · ቤቶ called "a spelling of ቤቱ"; it is the accusative (-o) of ቤቱ, object of ይሠርዕ, like ሑረቶ, ንብረቶ in unit 13. · Label corrected.
6. U14 · n · moderate · አበሰ called "the causative-form verb"; the initial አ is a root consonant, not a causative prefix. · Label corrected ("3mpl perfect; initial አ part of the root").
7. U14, U18, U19 · i (U13 n/a) · moderate (tense) · The imperfects describing Solomon's habitual character were rendered in a mixture of past and present across units 13–20 ("had pity", "ordered", "was like", "did not wish" against "bears", "opens", "judges"), and `l` and `i` disagreed in force. · i harmonised to the source's imperfect (habitual present) for the portrait: U14 "has pity… orders"; U18 "have come… do not wish"; U19 "is like"; U13 "how he answered" replaced by the noun phrase (see 15 below). The merchant's own acts (saw, marvelled, was astonished) stay past, as narrative imperfects, as the notes already explain.
8. U15 · i, n · moderate · ያክሞስሶሙ unknown, but the guess "bears gently(?)" was drawn from በየውሀት "with gentleness", so the manner was counted twice ("gently… with gentleness"); ይሤርሖን, which the note called uncertain, had no (?) in `i`. · i now "deals(?) with the fools with gentleness… sets(?) the maidservants in order with gentleness"; note says "deals with" is only a placeholder, drops the unsupported "quadriliteral" assertion, says Dillmann is unavailable.
9. U17 · n · moderate · ርኢዮ analysed as "gerund of ርእየ + -ኦ 'it'". ርኢዮ is the 3ms gerund by itself; its -ዮ is not an object suffix (the object is ዘንተ ኵሎ). · Label corrected; `l` "having-seen-it" → "having-seen".
10. U18 · n, i · moderate · ይእትቱ parsed as እተወ; a 3mpl jussive of እተወ would be ይእትዉ, so the form (ending -ቱ, last radical ተ) does not fit the lemma given. Sense only from the pairing with ይትገሐሡ. · Note now says the root is unplaced and the sense contextual; `i` marks "leave(?)". Dillmann unavailable.
11. U21 · n · moderate · ዕንቈ labelled "plural of ዕንቊ"; the plural is አዕናቍ, ዕንቈ is the accusative, used collectively. · Label corrected.
12. U19 · n · moderate (over-claim) · "recalls Isaiah 58:7 and Matthew 25:35–36 (food, drink, clothing, the sick)": Isaiah 58:7 has bread and clothing only, drink and the sick are Matthew's. · Reworded as "may recall" Matthew 25:35–36, and Isaiah 58:7 "in part" (bread, covering the naked); no quotation claimed.

### Findings refused or left, with reason
- U6 `i` "the one he called 'Queen of the South' is the queen of Ethiopia": a smoother rendering of ወዘይቤ (ዘ- "that which") is possible, but the sense is correct and the person/neuter difference does not change the claim. Left.
- U13 `i` "those under him" for እለ ይኤዝዞሙ: a mild gloss, but it is the natural reading of "those he commands". Left.
- U13 subject of ወነሥአ / ወወሀቦ (Solomon vs Tamrin): the `i` supplies "Solomon" as the note says; I judge it the better reading (Tamrin is named as the recipient, ለነጋዲ, so he is not the subject of ወወሀቦ), and the note already gives the other reading. Left.
- U8 በራእያኒ በላሕያኒ: the -ኒ on a word ending in -ya cannot be resolved here (the accusative of ራእይ would be ራእየ); the note's "both… and" is the plain sense. Left; flag for the glosser.
- U16 ጸቃውዐ "honeycomb(?)" and አዳም "comely(?)" (a "ruddy" sense for አዳም is possible): already marked uncertain, with the alternative given for አዳም; nothing better is available without Dillmann. Left.
- U11 በኀቤሁ "from him": already flagged as uncertain with the alternative; left.
- Unit 11 splitting: refused, no cut point (see above). Units 13 and 21 (41 words) are under the ~45 rule.
- Heading `i` "Chapter 21: …" matches ch17–20; the conventions' "ንግሥተ ሳባ = Queen of Sheba" does not apply because the text here says አዜብ; "Queen of the South" kept.
- Known-forms consistency: እግዚኣብሔር "God", ክብረ "glory", ዘኢይነቅዝ "which-not-it-rots", ኢትዮጵያ, ሰሎሞን, ኀበ, ማውታ (the "sense uncertain" in the known entry sits oddly with the confident "orphan" here, but እጓለ ማውታ as "orphan" is the established idiom) all agree with the published parts.

Gloss follow-ups for the glosser (not changed here): ህንደኬ (not ህንድ), ወአሕማረኒ (accusative + -ኒ), ርኢዮ (gerund), ይእትቱ (root unplaced), ዕንቈ (accusative), ቤቶ (accusative), ሣእሣአ (ś-series).

## Pass 2

Reviewer pass 2. Read: conventions.md, runbook.md, packet.md, units.json, gloss.json, novel-forms.json, known-forms.json, review.md, and the glossaries of kebra-nagast-ch1.json and kebra-nagast-ch17-20.json (house entries). No modern translation opened. Dillmann is unavailable: every word marked unresolved stays unresolved for that reason. All 212 novel-form entries and the 3 (now 6) `__broaden__` entries were checked against the text where each occurs and against Geʿez grammar (lemma shape, person/number/gender, tense, stem, state, proclitics and enclitics), the numerals by spoken words and by the build's own transliteration function (hooks.build_word), and gloss against `l`/`i` of units.json. Edits were made by script (gloss.json, units.json); `t` and `p` were verified identical to the packet before and after (1858 characters), gloss keys are exactly the 212 keys of novel-forms.json, and build and validate PASS (the built output was discarded; only gloss.json, units.json, review.md are changed).

Checks that came out clean: every other lemma is a genuine dictionary shape (verbs 3ms perfect; nouns singular absolute) and its parse fits the form, including ዘከርዋ, ይወቅሦሙ, ትስማዕ, ዘወሀባ, ወህባ (ወ is root-initial), ይሕንጽ, ይምጽኡ, ይንሥኡ, ይንሣእ, ወነገርዎ, ያምጽእ, ይሬእይዎ, ይኤዝዞሙ, ይምሕሮሙ, ትትፈቀር, ወትትሜነን, ኢያደሉ (causative of the III-w verb), ዘኢኮኑ, ወኢይከውኑ, the -ሁ/-ኦ suffixed noun lists of unit 13, and the proclitic/enclitic analyses (ወ ለ በ ዘ እም, -ሰ -ኒ -ሂ). Numeral number words are correct (21 ዕሥራ ወአሐዱ, 22 ዕሥራ ወክልኤቱ, 520 ሐምስቱ ምእት ወዕሥራ, 73 ሰብዓ ወሠለስቱ). Lemma is before ' — ' in every entry. Every `__broaden__` entry is the old entry whole + ' · ' + new text (checked by script against known-forms.json and, for the three older ones, kept so). l/i of units.json agree with the glosses apart from the items below.

### Refused or left, with reason
- Lemma style for tä-stem verbs: ተወልደ, ተፈቀረ, ተመነነ, ተነሥአ are given under the tä-stem, but ተገብረ and ወተመልአኩ-type entries in the house use the G root (ገብረ). Both are genuine dictionary heads (Dillmann lists derived stems under the root), so I did not churn lemmas; the parse in each entry names the stem.
- ወይሬኢ ወያነክር ወይትዐቀብ ያስተዐጽብ: glossed as narrative past, in agreement with `i` (pass 1 settled this); left.
- ወህባ: a ህ spelling of ሀ with ወ in the root; correct as the glosser has it.
- ብርት ባሕሩስ ብርዐ ጸቃውዕ ሣእሣአ ያክሞስሶሙ ይእትቱ: unresolved, Dillmann unavailable; the Amharic ብረት comparison under ብርት is the glosser's memory, unchecked, and is kept only as a hint marked (?).
- ሣእሣአ and ያክሞስሶሙ: lemma now the form as written (unidentified) rather than an invented dictionary head; if Dillmann is later consulted, re-lemmatise.
- ትትሜነን ተዋቀሠ ተፋትሐ መውአ አስተዐጸበ ተገሕሠ ላሕይ ሠርሐ: real-looking roots whose senses rest on context; all carry 'unconfirmed' or (?) and the units mark them in `i`.
